children: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Malaysia's consumer-price growth accelerated slightly in August, mainly due to stronger transport prices.

The consumer-price index rose 1.9% from a year earlier, the Department of Statistics said Friday. The pace was a tad faster than the 1.8% increase recorded in July, which was also the median estimate of economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal.
The near-term trajectory of crude oil prices remains an important upside risk to inflation, TA Securities analyst Farid Burhanuddin said in a recent note.

A sustained rise in oil prices could gradually feed through to domestic transport, logistics and production costs, raising the risk that headline inflation will exceed 2.0% in the coming months, he said.
However, targeted fuel subsidies and the absence of broad-based, demand-driven inflation should continue to provide some cushion, he added.
August's data showed that prices for food and nonalcoholic beverages--which together account for nearly 30% of the CPI basket--rose 1.9% from a year earlier.
Core inflation, which excludes volatile fresh-food prices and government-administered items, was 1.7%.
Compared with the previous month, consumer prices rose 0.3% in August, after no changes in July.
